angle: The fair battlecruiser grew a verified second engine — and the price of the upgrade is the issue's honest centerpiece: the combo database calls the new pairing infinite, our checker proved it stops at seven tokens, and the computed bracket floor went UP to 4 anyway — so this issue teaches you to pilot two engines and to argue your own bracket out loud, stack in hand: present the 4, argue the verified-reality 3.

teases: THE WEB, RESOLVED: a kill, an exile, a draw, a Forest, and a 5/5 that re-arms the trigger — Case A-005
BOUNDED AT SEVEN: the 'infinite' that raised our own bracket — and the stack that argues it back down
ONE-SIDED APOCALYPSE: 16 damage at one player while your herd takes 1 each — now all maindeck
10,000 GOLDFISH GAMES: mean cast 7.969 — and the verified engine that doesn't wait for him

departments.note: Full-bleed Gishath, Sun's Avatar art_crop (Zack Stella, LCI 229 — credit per §9). Masthead, Vol. 7, August 2026, $4.95 from issue.json verbatim. Authored tagline 'Seven damage, then the ground shakes.' under the logotype. The dominant coverline names stack 005's verified ping web because it is the most exciting checker-passed thing in the issue (§7.6) — the swap block's engine resolved on the exact board the block created. The 'PRESENT 4. ARGUE 3.' violator is the issue's honest centerpiece, not hype: the computed floor and the verified reality disagree, and the magazine says so on the front. Every tease maps to a delivered spread — no inflation.

Two buckets: THIS ISSUE'S DECK (First Turns through Judge's Desk highlights with their promises, not just titles) / EVERY ISSUE (standing departments). Reprint the full three-tier legend — ✓ checker-passed, ◆ seeded artifact, ★ labeled coaching. Flag the Kill spread and the FIVE case files A-001–A-005 as the issue's spine. One line of honest framing: 'The database calls one pairing in this deck infinite. Our checker proved it stops at seven. Our computed floor went up anyway. That is not a contradiction — that is the whole issue.'

departments.headline: THE WAVE AND THE WEB
departments.dek: Everyone at the table knows engine one: the eight-mana swing that free-rolls an army. Version 2 of this deck grew engine two — a checker-verified web that converts any Dinosaur's arrival into removal, ramp, and card draw without attacking at all. Here is how a battlecruiser learns to idle dangerously.
departments.body: Open on the question the reader already has: what is an 8-mana commander deck DOING for seven turns? V2's answer is: accruing. Move one — the wave, unchanged: Gishath connects, reveals cards equal to damage dealt, and free-rolls every Dinosaur among them; 34 bodies in 65 nonland spells keep the reveal dense, and Case A-001 prices one clean 7-damage hit at five bodies, three draws, and a discover at X=6. Move two — the honest cost is the number eight: mean cast turn 7.969 in the goldfish, 8.3% by turn 6 — attacked three ways: ramp (86.9% of games see ramp or fixing by turn 6, mean turn 2.044), the cheat/reducer layer (56.2% by turn 6: Urza's Incubator, Otepec Huntmaster, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual // Zoological Study, Descendants' Path), and the swap block's new big mana — Selvala, Heart of the Wilds taps for X equal to your greatest power and Regal Behemoth doubles every land tap under the crown; the simulator models neither, and how many turns they shave is deliberately unstated until an artifact prices it. Move three — the web, the v2 headline: with Forerunner of the Empire out, any Dinosaur entering offers an optional 1 damage to each creature, and Case A-005 resolved what one ping is worth on the exact post-swap board — an opponent's 1/1 dead to state-based actions, their 3/3 exiled under Trapjaw Tyrant, a Ripjaw Raptor draw, a Ranging Raptors Forest, and a Polyraptor copy that re-arms the trigger. The enrage engine is drawn by turn 6 in 72.6% of games — the deck's most reliable package. Close on the thesis: the swing is still timed like a combo turn — protection held, table's mana counted, sweeper assumed — but the deflection turns are no longer dead turns, and the morning after a wrath, the web restarts at two cards while the commander restarts at 8-plus-tax.

captions.Gishath, Sun's Avatar: **THE WHOLE DECK IN ONE TEXT BOX:** combat damage to a player reveals that many cards and free-rolls every Dinosaur among them — vigilance, trample, and haste mean the swing happens the turn he lands.
captions.Forerunner of the Empire: **THE HUB OF ENGINE TWO:** its ETB stacks any Dinosaur on top of your library, then every Dinosaur entry offers an optional 1 damage to each creature. It is a 1/3 Human Soldier — outside every tribal shield this deck owns, and its own ping hits it.
captions.Urza's Incubator: **THE REAL ACCELERANT:** Dinosaurs cost {2} less, turning your commander into a six-drop. The goldfish's 7.969 mean cast explicitly ignores this card — it is why your games run faster.

pilot_tips.text: Never plan to activate Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual with Unclaimed Territory's mana — it casts creature spells only, so it accelerates the cast plan and never the cheat plan; it cannot even cast the non-Dinosaur Forerunner.

departments.pull_quote: The trigger is still the wave. The web is what the tide does while you wait.

departments.headline: THE EIGHT-MANA GUARANTEE
departments.dek: What is guaranteed access worth when the card costs eight? Everything — this deck mulligans without ever looking for its win condition, because the win condition lives in the command zone. The catch is that the guarantee runs one way: the zone always offers Gishath, but the tax makes sure you can only really afford him once.
departments.body: Four teaching blocks. ZONE (✓, cite CR 903 command-zone access): the deck spends zero slots on backup win conditions it must draw, because the payoff is always castable from the zone — that is why Keep or Ship never asks 'do you have a threat?', and why v2's second engine is a value web, not a second wincon. THE TAX LADDER (✓, CR 903.8): first cast {8}, second {10}, third {12} — set against the goldfish's mean available mana of 6.46 on turn 8 and 7.321 on turn 10, the deck never organically reaches a second cast in the simulated window; Selvala and Regal Behemoth soften the ladder without repealing it. Conclusion, coached (★, strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance): protection is arithmetic, not caution — each uncovered removal spell costs the {2} tax plus a tempo turn, and two answered casts effectively ends your game. Flawless Maneuver costs zero with your commander out; it is THE swing-turn card. COLOR IDENTITY (✓, CR 903.4): Naya buys the best creatures and protection suite in the format and permanently locks out counterspells — your only stack interaction is Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard ping. THE CLOCK (✓, CR 903.10a): 7 power means exactly three connections for 21 commander damage — and because the reveal scales with damage dealt, the commander-damage plan and the value plan are the same swing; Boros Charm's double strike makes it two hits and a 14-card reveal. THE POLITICAL READ (★): Gishath is public information from turn zero; every sweeper at the table is being held for your pivot, not the token player's board.

captions.Gishath, Sun's Avatar: **THE COMMANDER FILE:** {5}{R}{G}{W}, Naya identity, goldfish mean cast 7.969 (median 8). Tax ladder: 8 → 10 → 12. The zone guarantees the card; the ladder is why you protect it instead of recasting it.
captions.Boros Charm: **THE CLOCK COMPRESSOR:** double strike turns a three-connection commander-damage kill into two — and doubles the reveal to 14 cards on the way.

pilot_tips.text: Hold Flawless Maneuver through your own attack, not just theirs — it costs zero while you control your commander, and the wrath you should be assuming comes after the trigger banks.

departments.pull_quote: The zone always offers him back. The ladder makes sure you can only afford him once.

departments.headline: THE HONEST NUMBER IS STILL EIGHT
departments.dek: Ten thousand seeded goldfish games on the post-swap list, and the headline finding did not move: mean commander cast turn 7.969, median 8, and 5,533 of 10,000 games never cast him by turn 10. What DID move is the second engine — and it is now the most reliable package in the deck.

callouts.title: THE COMMANDER CURVE
callouts.text: Cast-turn distribution: 8.3% by turn 6, the mode at turn 8 (1,332 games), and 55.3% of games never casting him by turn 10. The stated-assumptions box governs the read: the simulator models neither the cost reducers nor the swap block's Selvala and Regal Behemoth, so 7.969 is the ceiling of the problem, not your expectation.

callouts.title: THE ENGINE THAT DOESN'T WAIT
callouts.text: Enrage engine drawn: 72.6% of games by turn 6 (mean turn 2.543, 82.4% overall) — ahead of the Dinosaur payoff package at 62.3% and second only to raw ramp. The strategic frame calls this the single largest effect of the seven-card swap block, and Case A-005 shows what those cards do the moment they meet.

callouts.title: THE TWO-FRONT ATTACK ON EIGHT
callouts.text: Ramp or fixing drawn: 93.9% of games overall, 86.9% by turn 6, mean turn 2.044. Cost reducer or cheat piece drawn: 67.3% overall, 56.2% by turn 6, mean turn 3.039. The measured assault on the number eight — before the unmodeled big mana even enters the ledger.

callouts.title: THE MID-GAME SAG
callouts.text: Land-drop hit rate falls from 99.9% on turn 1 to 52.6% by turn 6, and mean available mana at turn 6 is just 5.486 — the deck ramps early, then leans on rocks, dorks, and now Selvala. Exactly the profile a mid-game sweeper punishes twice: board AND mana. The spell swaps changed none of this math — v3's answer was a tune, not a count: three basics became Windswept Heath, Commercial District, and Arctic Treeline, typed lands that widen what Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim, and Krosan Verge can fetch (Forest-card count 9 → 11) without touching the 21.

callouts.title: THE SWING-TURN KIT
callouts.text: Connection kit (haste or evasion for the big attacker) by turn 6: 51.4%. Protection held for the board by turn 6: 48.5%. Two coin-flips the pivot turn wants to win — the politics pages teach you to hide which ones you lost.

captions.Sol Ring: **MEASURED, NOT VIBES:** the opening-hand policy (keep 2–5 lands) kept 77.1% of first sevens with a mean of 0.28 mulligans — your floor, not your standard. Keep or Ship raises the bar.

pilot_tips.text: Read every power meter on this page knowing the simulator ignores this card — the 56.2% cheat-layer figure is drawn-by-turn-6, and any one of those pieces beats the 7.969 mean by turns.

departments.pull_quote: The simulation is only a simulation — and it says so in print, every issue.
departments.note: ◆ costume throughout; every figure verbatim from goldfish_metrics.json (v3, seed 42, sha fb3507e3b705). The stated-assumptions box is non-negotiable and sits adjacent to callout 1, not below the fold.

departments.headline: SEVEN DAMAGE, ONE PING
departments.dek: Engine one: a 7-damage connection the checker priced at five bodies, three draws, and a discover at X=6. Engine two: a single optional ping that kills, exiles, draws, ramps, and re-arms itself. Both resolved on real boards, both stamped PASS — and each with an ordering lesson that separates good pilots from lucky ones.

callouts.title: THE CONNECTION
callouts.text: Gishath attacks the open seat unblocked and deals 7. The trigger resolves: reveal seven — Regisaur Alpha, Ripjaw Raptor, Carnage Tyrant, and Ravenous Sailback are Dinosaur creature cards and hit the battlefield; the rest bottoms in a random order. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-001 →

callouts.title: ONE EVENT, NINE TRIGGERS
callouts.text: All four enter simultaneously as a single event. Regisaur Alpha's haste covers the newcomers, Garruk's Uprising sees three of them at power 4+, and Pantlaza, Sun-Favored offers its once-per-turn discover. Nine triggers, one controller — you — and you choose the order of every one.

callouts.title: THE ORDERING LESSON
callouts.text: Put Carnage Tyrant's Pantlaza trigger on top so the once-per-turn discover resolves first at X=6, and put Regisaur Alpha's token trigger on the bottom: the 3/3 arrives after the discover is spent, misses Garruk's Uprising at power 3, and re-triggers nothing. Stack it token-first and you are dared into a discover at X=3 instead. Net from one hit: five bodies, three cards, a discover at X=6 — one attack that replaces a turn cycle of casting.

callouts.title: THE PING
callouts.text: Engine two, on the exact board the swap block built. Itzquinth, Firstborn of Gishath enters; Forerunner of the Empire offers its optional ping and you say yes — 1 damage to each of the eight creatures on the battlefield, Forerunner included. State-based actions kill the opponent's 1/1 token BEFORE any trigger goes on the stack; then exactly four enrage triggers wait for your order. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-005 →

callouts.title: THE TARGETING LESSON
callouts.text: Trapjaw Tyrant's exile target is chosen as its trigger goes ON the stack — so the already-dead token can never eat the exile; the opponent's 3/3 does. Ranging Raptors fetches a tapped Forest, and a land entering is not a Dinosaur — Forerunner does not re-trigger. Ripjaw Raptor draws. Then Polyraptor's copy token ENTERS: a Dinosaur, and a genuinely new, genuinely optional Forerunner trigger. The web re-arms itself.

callouts.title: THE DECLINE
callouts.text: The 'you may' is chosen on resolution — and saying NO is a play. Declining banks the full yield at a cost of 1 damage marked on each of your creatures, all surviving, all clean again at cleanup. The throttle matters at scale too: Case A-003's verified maximum of SEVEN Polyraptor tokens is reached only by declining one intermediate ping — mashing yes caps you at six, and the chain self-terminates when Forerunner dies to its own third sweep.

callouts.title: THE THIRD WEAPON
callouts.text: Beside the two engines sits a verified one-sided apocalypse, now entirely maindeck: Blasphemous Act deals 13 to each creature, Temple Altisaur caps your OTHER Dinosaurs at 1 each, and Wrathful Raptors throws every point your team is dealt at a non-Dinosaur target — 16 total damage at one player while the opposing boards are already swept. One warning: the Act deals Forerunner the full 13. Fire it as a reset, never mid-engine. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-004 →

captions.Carnage Tyrant: **THE PRIORITY TRIGGER:** hexproof, uncounterable, and the biggest toughness in the reveal — its Pantlaza trigger is the one you resolve first, for a discover at X=6.
captions.Trapjaw Tyrant: **TARGETS ARE CHOSEN ON THE STACK:** a creature already dead to the ping can never be picked — and the exile is a hostage arrangement: the moment Trapjaw leaves, the prisoner comes home.
captions.Polyraptor: **ONE ENGINE, TWO VERDICTS:** behind Forerunner of the Empire's optional trigger it is a verified bounded burst and a self-re-arming web piece; with the benched Marauding Raptor it is a verified whole-table draw. The difference is two words of oracle text: 'you may.'

pilot_tips.text: Stack the biggest toughness's Pantlaza trigger to resolve first — the discover is once per turn, so spend it at X=6, never at X=3.
Count before you say yes — the ping hits Forerunner too (1 of 3), and declining one intermediate trigger is how the verified 7-token maximum is actually reached.

departments.pull_quote: THE DATABASE SAID INFINITE. THE CHECKER SAID: SEVEN — AND ONLY IF YOU SAY NO ONCE.
departments.note: Peak spread of the issue. Callouts 1–3 are engine one (Case A-001); callouts 4–6 are engine two (Cases A-005 and A-003); callout 7 is the maindeck sweep (Case A-004). Everything on these boards is in the 99 except A-001's stipulated reveal card Ravenous Sailback (since benched) — tag its image 'SINCE BENCHED' and carry the dossier's note that the ordering lesson is identical with any fourth Dinosaur. The refutation (A-002) and the floor conversation live at Judge's Desk; this spread points there exactly once, from the pull quote's shadow. Rules numbers stay in Judge's Desk; the narrative here carries the teaching.

departments.headline: THE MOST TELEGRAPHED DECK IN THE ROOM
departments.dek: Gishath is public information from turn zero, and v2 hands you a second announcement before the game even starts: a bracket report that says 4 over a verified stack that argues 3. How you run that conversation — and how you sequence two new attention magnets — is now as much a part of the deck as the mana base.

callouts.title: THE SIT-DOWN SCRIPT
callouts.text: Say it plainly, before the first shuffle: 'The report says 4 because the combo database tags Polyraptor plus Forerunner of the Empire as a two-card infinite. Our checker resolved that pairing on the exact board — it is bounded: a maximum of seven tokens, only by declining a trigger, self-terminating, stoppable at every link. The genuinely unbounded partner is deliberately not in this deck.' Present the 4, argue the verified 3, and let the table decide. Never sandbag the label and then drop seven raptors on turn six — the conversation IS the bracket system working.

callouts.title: THE NEW TELL
callouts.text: V1 was ignorable until seven mana. V2 becomes a problem the moment Forerunner of the Empire stands next to any raptor — and experienced tables answer engines at the hub: a 1/3 Human Soldier outside every tribal shield eats the first Swords on sight. Deploy him the turn you can use him, not before, or bait the removal first.

callouts.title: TWO CROWNS PAINT TARGETS
callouts.text: Regal Behemoth makes you the monarch the turn it lands — real draw, and a crown every aggro deck at the table is now obliged to take. Selvala's draw clause is symmetric: whoever plays the table's new biggest creature gets the card, opponents included. Sequence both when your own curve dominates the board, not while you are still posturing.

callouts.title: THE THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: The moment the trigger banks — five bodies, three draws, a discover at X=6, per Case A-001 — you are the archenemy no matter how you posture. From that board, plan to end the game within one table rotation: the ping web is your board control while Overwhelming Stampede or a second connection closes. The table will not give you two.

captions.Rogue's Passage: **THE BLOCKER MATH:** a 4-toughness chump eats lethal assignment and shaves your reveal from 7 to 3 even through trample. Passage's {4} buys a guaranteed 7-card reveal and zero blocker interaction — it beats the pump whenever a real blocker exists.
captions.Worldly Tutor: **THE LOUDEST INSTANT IN THE DECK:** an end-step tutor the turn before eight mana tells three opponents exactly when the ground shakes. Cast it committed or not at all.

pilot_tips.text: Spend pump mana only into genuinely open lanes — the reveal scales with damage DEALT, so a pumped swing into a chump block converts to nothing while Rogue's Passage converts to seven cards.

departments.pull_quote: You hold protection 48.5% of the time. The table doesn't know which 48.5% — keep it that way.

departments.headline: NINE MANA, TWO BLUE SEATS
departments.dek: Two boards from real Gishath turns. In the first, your commander is resolving with one mana open and a lane that exists this turn only. In the second, nine triggers are about to hit the stack and only one order is right. Commit to your line before you turn the page — the recommendations wait below the branches.

callouts.title: PUZZLE ONE: SWING OR HOLD?
callouts.text: Turn 8, precombat main. Gishath was cast for eight — first cast, no tax — and is on the stack with one mana still open; Rogue's Passage is NOT affordable this turn. Seat A is Azorius flash control with two blue up. One seat cannot block profitably. Do you swing now on one free trick, or untap into the covered line? Three branches, then our answer.

callouts.title: PUZZLE TWO: ORDER THE CASCADE
callouts.text: Combat damage step: Gishath connected for 7, and the reveal put Regisaur Alpha, Ripjaw Raptor, Carnage Tyrant, and Ravenous Sailback onto the battlefield under Pantlaza, Sun-Favored and Garruk's Uprising. Nine triggers, one once-per-turn discover, and you choose every position. Which trigger goes on top — and which goes to the bottom?

captions.Flawless Maneuver: **THE FREE INSURANCE:** the card that changes puzzle one's math — with your commander on the battlefield it costs {0}, which means holding open mana is not the same thing as holding an answer.

departments.pull_quote: Assume every held answer appears the moment the 8-drop hits the stack — then count what you can pay for.
departments.note: Renders from decisions/001-swing-or-hold-gishath.json and decisions/002-pantlaza-discover-order.json — both rationales are v2-synced (001 cites the goldfish mean and the Selvala/Behemoth softened-but-not-repealed recast math). Two stipulation footnotes the renderer must carry: 001's authored board includes Drover of the Mighty and 002's reveal includes Ravenous Sailback, both since benched by the swap block — a stipulated board is a stipulated board, and the lessons are unchanged, but the footnote says so honestly. Hard rule: recommendation strictly after the branches, and neither headline nor board copy may telegraph 'swing' as correct in puzzle one. Puzzle two deliberately echoes the Kill's ordering lesson — reading the spread first is not cheating, it's the curriculum.

departments.headline: WHO HOLDS THE WRATH FOR YOU
departments.dek: Every archetype at the table prices your deck the same way: one big turn, then a reckoning. Four threat files on who actually collects — every named out already sleeved, plus the one own-goal the new engine makes possible.

callouts.title: SWEEPER CONTROL — THREAT: SEVERE
callouts.text: Still the worst frame: the Gishath trigger builds a one-wrath board and deploy-in-waves is structurally unavailable. Outs: Flawless Maneuver and Boros Charm beat destroy-based sweepers; Heroic Intervention adds hexproof; Akroma's Will covers both with the commander out; Eerie Interlude is the only out to -X/-X, sacrifice, and exile wraths — but it abandons your tokens, Polyraptor copies included: the desperation line. What v2 adds is the morning after: the web restarts at two cards — Forerunner plus any Dinosaur — while the commander restarts at 8-plus-tax, and Ranging Raptors' lands plus Ripjaw's draws stay banked. Two riders: the board-wide instants are ALSO the only cover Forerunner has, and your own Blasphemous Act deals him the full 13 — fire it as a reset, never mid-engine.

callouts.title: FAST COMBO — THREAT: SEVERE
callouts.text: Still the bad seat: zero counterspells in Naya, six spot-removal slots, a clock starting near the 7.969 mean. Outs: Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, and Beast Within go at enablers on sight; Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard mode is instant-speed reach; Belbe's Portal deploys Gishath at instant speed the end step before your combat. What v2 adds: a turn-5 Forerunner-plus-Polyraptor board threatens real damage a full rotation before Gishath — the race no longer waits for the commander. Held answers rot — spend now.

callouts.title: STAX — THREAT: HIGH
callouts.text: Taxes hit an 8-drop harder than anyone at the table, so the fight is over your cheat layer: mulligan toward the 56.2% (Urza's Incubator, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual // Zoological Study, Descendants' Path). The web is your best under-stax posture — it runs on creature ETBs, not activations or big casts — and Selvala's single activation makes big mana tax-resilient. Aim Thrashing Brontodon, Beast Within, and Austere Command at the piece that turns the cheat layer off, not the scariest permanent. Remember: neither typal land can even cast the non-Dinosaur Forerunner.

callouts.title: ENRAGE-HOSTILE BOARDS — THREAT: MODERATE
callouts.text: Deathtouch and first-strike tables invert your combat enrage: Temple Altisaur's prevention leaves 1 through, and 1 deathtouch damage still destroys — never offer Ripjaw Raptor or Polyraptor into those blocks. But v2 makes the web the answer: Forerunner's ping is YOUR source, so their deathtouchers never touch your enrage bodies; Trapjaw Tyrant's trigger exiles the deathtoucher outright (Case A-005); Rogue's Passage dodges the block entirely. One husbandry rule: the ping hits your own hub — three pings in one turn kill Forerunner, so count before the third yes.

captions.Eerie Interlude: **THE DESPERATION OUT:** the only answer to exile and -X/-X wraths — but it abandons your tokens and returns the bodies at end step. Whether Pantlaza's discover fires off the return still needs a stack scenario, so don't count on the rebate.

pilot_tips.text: Against combo, spend Trumpeting Carnosaur from your hand as the discard ping at their enabler — the 7/6 body is a luxury the bad seat cannot afford.

departments.pull_quote: Every sweeper at the table is being held for YOUR pivot turn — plan like you can see it.

departments.headline: SIXTY-FIVE SPELLS, TWO ENGINES
departments.dek: Why does a deck about one trigger need ninety-nine cards? Because every slot either accelerates toward the trigger, cheapens it, protects it, rigs it, cashes it in — or, new this issue, feeds the web that works while the trigger waits. Name a card's job and you know exactly when to spend it.
departments.body: Card-tile grid grouped by job, ranked within group, prose from manual_prose.card_roles. Groups, in reading order: THE PAYOFF CORE (Gishath, Sun's Avatar; Pantlaza, Sun-Favored; Descendants' Path; Etali, Primal Storm; Carnage Tyrant; the 34-body herd — lead with the load-bearing five, tile the rest); THE WEB (new group, all seven pieces with their case-file pointers: Forerunner of the Empire the hub, Polyraptor, Ranging Raptors, Ripjaw Raptor, Trapjaw Tyrant, Wrathful Raptors, Temple Altisaur — plus Itzquinth, Firstborn of Gishath as the verified arming Dinosaur); THE ACCELERANT LAYER (21 lands — tuned in v3: Windswept Heath, Commercial District, and Arctic Treeline in for three basics, typed duals that deepen the fetch ramp and drop the basics to 14 — plus Cultivate/Kodama's Reach/Nature's Lore/Skyshroud Claim, five rocks, the dorks, the new big mana pair Selvala, Heart of the Wilds and Regal Behemoth, Mirari's Wake, and the cheat/reducer tier: Urza's Incubator, Otepec Huntmaster, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual // Zoological Study, Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People); THE PROTECTION SUITE (Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm, Akroma's Will, Eerie Interlude — with the new second duty: only these cover Forerunner); INTERACTION (Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, Beast Within, Triumphant Chomp, Bronzebeak Foragers, Thrashing Brontodon, Blasphemous Act, Austere Command, Wakening Sun's Avatar); THE RIGGING (Congregation at Dawn, Worldly Tutor, Enlightened Tutor — the two Game Changers that set the floor's first driver — plus Forerunner's own ETB, which stacks a Dinosaur on top); THE CONNECTION KIT (Rogue's Passage, Kessig Wolf Run, Hunter's Insight, Overwhelming Stampede). Then the separate labeled strip: THE BENCH — 21 cards whose job changed this issue from step-up package to answer box: fourteen conditional answers, the seven bodies the block sent down, one spare Wakening Sun's Avatar, one live trial, and one warning label; pointer to Upgrade Watch.

captions.Descendants' Path: **THE REPEATABLE CHEAT:** every upkeep, a revealed Dinosaur gets cast free — and with 34 bodies the hit rate is real. Casting, not putting, matters for cast triggers.
captions.Wakening Sun's Avatar: **READ THE FINE PRINT:** it wipes non-Dinosaurs only if you CAST it from your hand — a Gishath free-roll or Portal activation gets the body and skips the wrath. And note the friendly fire: Forerunner of the Empire is a Human, so your own Avatar cast kills your web's hub.
captions.Zacama, Primal Calamity: **THE CAST-ONLY REFUND:** its lands-untap clause triggers on casting from your hand, so a free-roll delivers the removal engine but not the mana rebate.
captions.Secluded Courtyard: **READ THE CLAUSE, NOT THE PHRASE:** its mana casts Dinosaur spells AND activates abilities of Dinosaur sources — so it pays Zacama, but never Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual.
captions.Krosan Verge: **THE TUNE'S TARGET DIET:** it fetches a Forest card and a Plains card — not just basics — and v3's Arctic Treeline is both types on one land: exactly what the Verge wants to find.

pilot_tips.text: Cast Congregation at Dawn before a Gishath connection, not after — three creatures stacked on top turns the reveal from a lottery into a delivery.

departments.pull_quote: Roughly 40% of the deck makes or reduces mana. That is not padding — that is the price of the number eight.
departments.note: Ranked, not encyclopedic (anti-pattern: completionism). Six cards have no role tag (Descendants' Path, Eerie Interlude, Hunter's Insight, Overwhelming Stampede, Rishkar's Expertise, Triumphant Chomp) — the taxonomy lacks patterns, not the cards functions; the grid places them by their real jobs and says so in a footnote.

departments.headline: SEVENTY-SIX HANDS, ONE HERD
departments.dek: Nobody painted this deck — seventy-six people did. Across 110 card entries there is no standout hand, and that breadth is the story: a tribe assembled across decades of sets, with the biggest single contribution just six cards wide — and the swap block quietly reshuffled whose work is sleeved.
departments.body: Breadth feature, per the analysis: standout is null and the lead cluster is six cards, so no curation story gets invented. Hero image: the commander — Gishath, Sun's Avatar by Zack Stella (LCI 229), credited per §9. Lead cluster: Simon Dominic, 6 entries, every one a Dinosaur or Dinosaur spell — and the swap block cut his cluster straight down the middle: three maindeck (Curious Altisaur, Ranging Raptors, Triumphant Chomp — the block promoted his Ranging Raptors) and three benched (Apex Altisaur, Kinjalli's Sunwing, Silverclad Ferocidons — and benched his Sunwing); the gallery labels the bench cards honestly. Second: Tyler Jacobson, 5 entries — with the honest footnote that two of them are the same card, the maindeck-plus-spare pair of Wakening Sun's Avatar, so his distinct-card count is four; his Selvala, Heart of the Wilds is now maindeck. Also worth noting strip: Daarken painted two of the three pieces of the verified one-sided sweep, both maindeck (Blasphemous Act and Temple Altisaur — April Prime painted the third, Wrathful Raptors) plus Otepec Huntmaster; Dan Murayama Scott painted both the format's plainest rock and the web's hub (Arcane Signet, Forerunner of the Empire); Sam Burley painted both Pantlaza, Sun-Favored and Secluded Courtyard; Mark Tedin's pair (Belbe's Portal, City of Brass) spans a quarter-century of the game. The v3 land tune's footnote: it added two new names to the roster (Alexander Forssberg's Windswept Heath, Julian Kok Joon Wen's Commercial District) and made Alayna Danner a two-entry hand — Arctic Treeline beside Path of Ancestry. Art File facts: 110 entries, 121 copies, 76 artists, 0 accessories, 0 foils, 0 borderless; frame effects run to 10 legendary crowns. Counting note printed in spirit: per-entry is the honest basis — Forest is one entry despite 7 copies, or the count would inflate Maojin Lee.

captions.Curious Altisaur: **THE LEAD HAND:** Simon Dominic's six Dinosaurs make him this deck's widest contributor — and the swap block split his cluster three maindeck, three bench.
captions.Forerunner of the Empire: **THE HUB PAINTER:** Dan Murayama Scott's two entries are the deck's plainest artifact and its most load-bearing creature — Arcane Signet and the Human Soldier every verified web line runs through.

departments.pull_quote: The biggest hand in a 110-card collection painted exactly six of them.
departments.note: No drop_runs, no roster overlap flagged — there is no bought-whole product story to tell and none is invented. Counts are recomputed by the renderer from artist-credits; the plan supplies only the framing and prose.

departments.headline: MULLIGAN FOR AN ENGINE — EITHER ENGINE
departments.dek: The goldfish's loose policy — keep any seven with two to five lands — kept 77.1% of hands. That is your floor, not your standard: your commander is guaranteed, so every mulligan question is really an acceleration question — and v2 made a whole second class of hand keepable. Four hands; make your call before reading the verdicts.

callouts.title: HAND ONE
callouts.text: Forest, Plains, Command Tower, Sol Ring, Cultivate, Urza's Incubator, Carnage Tyrant. VERDICT: KEEP — easily. Ramp on curve plus the deck's scarcest resource: a cheat/reducer piece is drawn by turn 6 in only 56.2% of games, and this hand already holds the headline one.

callouts.title: HAND TWO
callouts.text: Ghalta, Primal Hunger; Zacama, Primal Calamity; Etali, Primal Storm; Vaultborn Tyrant; two Forests, Mountain. VERDICT: SHIP. All payoff, no engine — mean available mana at turn 6 is 5.486 and the land-drop hit rate has already sagged to 52.6% by then. The deck does not organically climb to eight; hands like this ask it to.

callouts.title: HAND THREE
callouts.text: Unclaimed Territory, Jetmir's Garden, Alpine Meadow, Belbe's Portal, Selvala, Heart of the Wilds, Regisaur Alpha, Boros Charm. VERDICT: SHIP — and know why. Every land enters tapped or restricted; nothing deploys on time, Selvala's {G}{G} has no untapped green on turn 2, and Unclaimed Territory can never activate the Portal this hand is banking on — nor cast the Elf it's carrying.

callouts.title: HAND FOUR
callouts.text: Forest, Mountain, Forerunner of the Empire, Ranging Raptors, Kodama's Reach, Garruk's Uprising, Ripjaw Raptor. VERDICT: KEEP — the hand class v2 invented. The web curve is a real game plan on its own: enrage pieces are drawn by turn 6 in 72.6% of games (mean turn 2.543), and Case A-005 prices what this board does every turn while Gishath waits. Eyes open: the hub is a 1/3 Human outside every tribal shield — deploy him the turn he works.

captions.Cultivate: **THE STANDARD-BEARER:** 86.9% of games see ramp or fixing by turn 6, mean turn 2.044 — a keepable hand almost always has it, so a hand without it is below your deck's own average.

pilot_tips.text: Count Ranging Raptors as ramp when you keep a web hand — the Forests it fetches live on lands, safe from the wrath that erases every dork.

departments.pull_quote: Your win condition is in the command zone. Your mulligan is about everything else.
departments.note: ★ verdicts grounded in ◆ figures — cite 77.1% keep rate, 0.28 mean mulligans, and the target rates exactly. Hands are authored drills, deterministic, drawn from manual_prose.mulligan's v2 ship/keep classes (all cards named are maindeck in the applied build).

departments.headline: THE UPGRADE ALREADY HAPPENED
departments.dek: Most upgrade columns are shopping lists. This one is a receipt: seven swaps, applied only after five checker-passed stacks priced what they buy — plus the eighth swap we refused, the one live trial still gated behind a scenario, and a bench whose job just changed from step-up package to answer box.

callouts.title: THE BLOCK
callouts.text: Applied 2026-07-28 (HISTORY.md, decklist fb99de15993a). IN: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds; Regal Behemoth; Forerunner of the Empire; Polyraptor; Wrathful Raptors; Ranging Raptors; Trapjaw Tyrant. OUT, to the bench: Ravenous Sailback, Verdant Sun's Avatar, Goring Ceratops, Zetalpa, Primal Dawn, Earthshaker Dreadmaw, Drover of the Mighty, Kinjalli's Sunwing. Seven fair or redundant bodies traded for a verified second engine plus the acceleration the deck's turn-8 mean cast demanded — and nothing moved until a passed stack said what it does.

callouts.title: THE BRANCH NOT TAKEN
callouts.text: Swap eight would have been Marauding Raptor for Otepec Huntmaster — declined on Case A-002's verdict, and now blocked outright: with Polyraptor maindeck, sleeving Marauding Raptor imports the verified mandatory loop that draws the whole game directly into the 99. The deck holds no sacrifice outlet, no exit. Promotion requires Polyraptor leaving the 99 or a free loop-breaker arriving first. One or the other. Never both.

callouts.title: THE ONE LIVE TRIAL
callouts.text: Bellowing Aegisaur in for Pugnacious Hammerskull, web-centric pods only: its v1 blocker — 'a 6-mana 5/5 that needs someone else to hurt it' — is resolved, because the someone else is now maindeck and verified, and every optional ping would read 'a +1/+1 counter on each other creature you control,' hardening the fragile hub. But Aegisaur never grows itself and eats every ping, so its survival budget mid-burst is unverified — the swap stays conditional until its named stack scenario runs.

callouts.title: THE HONEST LEDGER
callouts.text: The price of the block on paper: the computed floor moved 3 → 4 solely on the database's infinite tag for Polyraptor + Forerunner of the Empire — the pairing Case A-003 verified as bounded at seven tokens. The bench holds no Game Changers, so nothing down there moves a bracket either way. And the obsolescence index still offers almost nothing tuned to typal fit — its one actionable note remains the strict ramp family (Three Visits, Farseek beside the Nature's Lore class already here), and we say so out loud.

captions.Selvala, Heart of the Wilds: **THE HEADLINE PROMOTION:** a 3-mana engine aimed at the deck's defining problem — with the political rider that her draw clause is symmetric, so sequence her when your own curve dominates the table.
captions.Marauding Raptor: **THE WARNING LABEL:** its 2-damage ping is mandatory, Polyraptor's copy trigger is mandatory, and 2 never kills a fresh 5/5 — the verified outcome, with no exit in this deck, is a draw for the whole table.

pilot_tips.text: Never sleeve Marauding Raptor into this 99 while Polyraptor is maindeck — the loop is mandatory, the deck holds no exit, and the verified outcome is a draw for the whole table.

departments.pull_quote: Nothing moved off this bench until a passed stack said what it actually does — five verifications, seven swaps, one refusal.
departments.note: ◆ department rendering sideboard_analysis.json (v2): one live trial swap, twenty-one long-term verdicts, nine candidate lines — four verified with dossier pointers (A-002/A-003/A-004/A-005), five flagged 'needs a stack scenario' (Wrathful × web, Selvala/Behemoth quantification, Aegisaur budget, Silverclad edicts, Apex fight-chain) and never asserted. Single violator: 'ONE PAIR MUST NEVER MEET!' on the exclusion panel.

departments.headline: PROVE IT
departments.dek: Five cases this issue — and a fight between our own database and our own checker that the checker wins. The combo DB tags one maindeck pairing infinite, and that tag alone computes a bracket floor of 4; Case A-003 proved the pairing stops at seven. Both facts print here in full, because the floor conversation is yours to run at the table.

callouts.title: CASE A-001 — THE TRIGGER CASCADE
callouts.text: Gishath connects for 7: what one reveal actually unleashes, and why trigger order decides whether the discover lands at X=6 or X=3. VERDICT: PASS, 2 iterations.

callouts.title: CASE A-002 — THE DRAW-MACHINE
callouts.text: Marauding Raptor + Polyraptor: infinite tokens, or a mandatory loop with no exit? VERDICT: PASS, 2 iterations — the loop draws the game for the whole table unless an opponent chooses to break it. The verdict that stopped the swap block at seven.

callouts.title: CASE A-003 — THE BOUNDED BURST
callouts.text: Forerunner of the Empire + Polyraptor: maximum 7 tokens, safe stop at every link, self-terminating — and the maximum requires DECLINING a trigger. VERDICT: PASS, 1 iteration. This is the substance of the argue-3 case against the computed floor of 4.

callouts.title: CASE A-004 — THE ONE-SIDED ACT
callouts.text: Wrathful Raptors + Blasphemous Act + Temple Altisaur: your Dinosaurs dealt 1 each, the shield takes its own 13 and still redirects it via last known information, 16 total to one player. VERDICT: PASS, 2 iterations.

callouts.title: CASE A-005 — THE PING WEB
callouts.text: One optional ping on the applied board: a 1/1 dead to state-based actions before any trigger stacks, a 3/3 exiled under Trapjaw Tyrant, a Ripjaw draw, a Ranging Raptors Forest, and a Polyraptor copy whose entry re-arms the trigger. VERDICT: PASS, 1 iteration.

(2) A-001's stipulation note: the authored reveal includes Ravenous Sailback, since benched — the ordering lesson is identical with any fourth Dinosaur.

rhythm_notes: Canonical alternation holds without forced breathers: By the Numbers (dense analysis, now five callouts because v2's data story has two headlines) hands off to The Kill, the issue's peak — restaged as a two-engine spread where callouts 1–3 (the cascade) crest into 4–6 (the ping web) with callout 7 as the coda, everything on the boards maindeck so the spread no longer needs bench tags, only one 'SINCE BENCHED' image flag. Politics follows as reflection and carries the issue's signature beat — the sit-down script — in words, not numbers. What's Your Play spikes participation, Know Your Enemy settles into reference, and The 99 (browsing) plus Featured Artist (appreciation, the art break) are the deliberate two-spread cool-down before Keep or Ship re-engages with the drill — whose hand four now teaches the new keepable class instead of repeating hand one's lesson. Upgrade Watch runs lighter than its v1 counterpart despite bigger news, because a receipt is calmer than a forecast: four callouts, one violator, drama concentrated on the refused eighth swap. Judge's Desk is opt-in density at the back, now carrying the floor sidebar beside A-003 so the argument and its evidence share a page; the Back Page closes the loop. Pun budget spent: 'THE WAVE AND THE WEB', 'SEVENTY-SIX HANDS, ONE HERD', 'THE UPGRADE ALREADY HAPPENED' as a straight-faced twist on the genre, and the back page's counting beat — four, all in furniture.

Wrathful Raptors × the Forerunner ping web is the frame's named unresolved rules question — both halves are maindeck but no stack has run them on one board; until it does, the manual may not say whether a ping with Wrathful out still feeds the enrage engine or converts to reach. One rules domain, one scenario.

The Bellowing Aegisaur survival-budget scenario gates the issue's single live trial swap; the Silverclad Ferocidons edict line and the Apex Altisaur fight-chain are the other two unverified composites — each is its own scenario per the scope rule.

Selvala/Regal Behemoth acceleration is unquantified — the goldfish models neither card, so every department says 'ceiling of the problem' instead of an expected cast turn; a goldfish extension or worked sequencing scenario would replace the hedge with a number.
Eerie Interlude's end-step return vs Pantlaza's once-per-turn discover still needs a stack scenario — Know Your Enemy hedges the rebate in a caption.
Congregation at Dawn / Worldly Tutor rigging a Gishath reveal is still printed as setup coaching only; a stack scenario would let The Kill state the rigged-reveal line as fact.

The bracket engine does not consult passing stacks (hapatra and now gishath are two precedents) — every artifact hand-carries 'present 4, argue verified-reality 3 (stack 003)'; an engine that consumes stack verdicts would retire the caveat, and the strategy DB has no doctrine section for reconciling computed bracket signals with verified-bounded lines, which this issue's centerpiece leans on.

Two stipulated boards cite since-benched cards — decision 001's board includes Drover of the Mighty and decision/stack 002's-and-001's reveal includes Ravenous Sailback; both are legal stipulations flagged with renderer footnotes, but re-authoring against the applied 99 would remove the footnotes entirely.
Strategy DB holes felt while writing (logged by the frame): typal construction, enrage/self-damage engines as a resource, cheat-into-play as an archetype axis, top-of-library stacking discipline.
No bench card has an EDHREC rank, so every Upgrade Watch verdict rests on deck fit plus the five stacks, not popularity; a data refresh with ranks would let the department cite demand.
Featured Artist has no standout (lead cluster 6 of 110 entries) — the breadth story runs as planned; noted so no future editor invents a curation narrative.
